title: Real-time cellular and molecular vision of the intact operative field

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a surgical imaging system that continuously identifies cells, tissue types or molecular targets across the intact working field, including tissue at the plane being dissected. The surgeon would receive a spatial display broad and fast enough to guide an operation without removing a specimen for each reading. Its scope would be defined by the tissues and targets it can identify, the area and depth it covers, and how reliably it updates during surgery. This is a proposed capability, not an achievement established by the supplied evidence.

The motivating gap is the distance between obtaining microscopic information at selected locations and maintaining useful microscopic guidance across a changing surgical field. The supplied confocal literature documents small imaging fields, limited penetration and interference from movement and blood. The brain-tumor study also describes wide-field 5-ALA fluorescence as providing less cellular architectural detail than confocal imaging. These examples explain the goal without establishing that all existing imaging fits one classification or that every fluorescence technique has the same limitations.

Conceptual distinction: resolving cell-sized structures is only one component. A useful display must also establish what those structures are, or which molecular targets are present, with validated specificity. Cellular appearance, molecular identity, tissue perfusion and preserved physiological function are different measurements. The proposed system need not measure all of them, but its display must make clear which information it actually provides.

significance.text: If achieved, this capability would extend microscopic assessment from selected spots to the field that guides dissection. This matters particularly where tumor and normal tissue intermingle: the supplied brain-tumor study identifies infiltrating glioma margins as difficult to discriminate and interpret. Continuous, validated identification could reduce dependence on choosing the right biopsy location and could map detectable residual disease while the operation remains open. Those are conditional consequences of the proposed capability; fewer sampling errors and better diagnostic decisions would still require clinical demonstration.

Conditional impact synthesis: validated identification of nerves, vessels and tissue boundaries could help surgeons select a dissection plane and avoid critical structures. The benefit would depend on performance in the particular tissue, including whether the relevant boundary lies within imaging depth and remains visible during manipulation. Recognizing a nerve does not establish that it still conducts, and recognizing a vessel does not establish adequate blood flow. Safer dissection, improved function and better patient outcomes would therefore be additional findings to demonstrate.

Better visualization would not itself remove every infiltrating malignant cell or prevent recurrence. The brain-tumor study discusses the difficulty of complete clearance in highly infiltrative disease and calls for further evaluation of resection and survival outcomes. Disease below detection limits, beyond imaging depth or outside the operative field would remain important boundaries. Complete selective removal while preserving an organ, and control of disease elsewhere in the body, require capabilities beyond this imaging advance.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central unsolved integration is obtaining useful coverage, depth, specificity and speed together under operative conditions. The supplied gastrointestinal confocal review documents microscopic fields and superficial penetration, including the inability to see deeper structures in the described applications. The brain-tumor study reports that scanning speed limited rapid inspection of large areas. Improving image quality at one contact point would address only part of the proposed field-scale capability.

Blood and motion are demonstrated engineering obstacles. In the brain-tumor study, more than half of acquired images were uninterpretable, commonly because of motion distortion or obscuration by clumped red blood cells. A system intended to guide ongoing dissection would need to maintain useful coverage through these disturbances, or promptly indicate where information is unavailable. High diagnostic accuracy on selected interpretable images cannot by itself establish that the working field is reliably visible.

Engineering synthesis: the display must also remain aligned with tissue as the surgeon moves, deforms or removes it. Identification must distinguish the intended targets from nearby normal tissue, including ambiguous transition zones, and must communicate uncertainty without creating false confidence. Combining microscopy, molecular probes and image interpretation may contribute, but the supplied evidence does not establish a particular architecture that solves these requirements. Image acquisition, interpretation and display must together fit the pace of the intended operation.

current_state.text: A gastrointestinal probe-based confocal laser endomicroscopy review published on November 3, 2025 reports approximately 1 µm lateral resolution and an imaging depth of approximately 55–70 µm for the systems summarized. It describes pCLE as an adjunct rather than a routine standard and identifies superficial penetration, narrow fields, operator dependence and interpretation variability as limitations. Its body also discusses superficial imaging up to approximately 250 µm, so 55–70 µm should not be treated as a universal depth limit for all confocal systems. These findings concern gastrointestinal applications rather than an exhaustive survey of surgical imaging. The supplied review assessed retained article text; figures were not visually inspected.

A single-institution brain-tumor feasibility study published on May 14, 2025 enrolled 50 patients during 2020–2023 and evaluated intraoperative in vivo confocal imaging with a handheld system. Real-time neuropathology consultation occurred in 27 cases. The reported mean of 10.5 seconds measures time from the start of scanning to the first interpretable image, not time to a completed diagnostic consultation. The study demonstrates acquisition of cellular tissue images at selected operative locations; it does not demonstrate continuous identification across the whole field during dissection.

The same study's abstract and results prose report 93% sensitivity and 81% specificity against permanent histology, whereas Table 3 reports 92% sensitivity, with a reported interval of 83–96%, and 80% specificity, with an interval of 61–91%, for all CLE specimens. The supplied review found no explanation reconciling these overall estimates. Glioma-margin specificity was 50%, compared with 93% in the core, underscoring that performance at the clinically difficult boundary can differ substantially from performance within a lesion. The article also contains discrepancies between abstract and body counts of images and regions of interest, leaving exact denominators unresolved.

More than half of acquired images in that study were uninterpretable, most commonly because of motion or clumped red blood cells. This statement concerns individual images; it does not mean that more than half of patients or sampled regions yielded no usable image. Regions with non-interpretable imaging were excluded from the diagnostic analysis. The retained full discussion supports these findings directly, superseding the earlier research's reliance on a search excerpt. Image yield and diagnostic accuracy therefore describe different aspects of performance and must be considered together.

The earlier research identifies a stimulated Raman histology study attributed to Nohman and colleagues, reportedly published online on November 17, 2024. It describes label-free production of hematoxylin-and-eosin-like specimen images in minutes, a 70-case brain-tumor cohort, an AUC of 0.77 for diagnostic agreement and a workflow testing one specimen at a time. These remain reported claims rather than verified findings in this record: the only retained PubMed extraction contained a cookie notice, so the supplied evidence review could not confirm the article's identity or scientific content. That extraction failure does not establish that the reported findings are false.

Evidence boundary: the supplied materials establish dated confocal demonstrations and their limitations, but contain no usable freshness-search results establishing the state of the entire field as of November 1, 2026. They therefore support the proposed research goal without proving that no other modality or subsequent development meets some or all of its scope.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: during an open or minimally invasive human operation, an integrated system should display validated cellular or molecular identities across a continuous field large enough to guide the intended dissection, including tissue at the cutting plane, without requiring specimen removal for every reading. The protocol should specify field dimensions, depth, update rate, end-to-end latency and how coverage is maintained as the field changes. Isolated contact-probe readings or a virtual stain of an excised specimen would not alone demonstrate this scope. These are proposed criteria, not established regulatory thresholds.
completion_criteria.label: Validated cellular or molecular identities span the operative cutting plane

completion_criteria.text: Proposed validation: a prespecified human series should compare the display with location-matched histology for the tissues relevant to the intended operations, including nerve, vessel, tumor and normal parenchyma where applicable. Tissue-specific performance targets should be set before evaluation, with particular attention to margins and mixed tissue. The study should report unavailable and uninterpretable regions alongside diagnostic results, rather than judging the system only where it produces a usable image. Location-matched histology and the exclusion of uninterpretable regions in the supplied confocal study provide practical motivation for this design.
completion_criteria.label: Location-matched human histology comparisons report tissue-specific performance and unusable regions

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and boundaries: independent teams should reproduce performance across the intended operators, procedures and operative conditions, including blood, motion and tissue deformation. Reports should identify which targets, tissue states, depths and field sizes were tested, how long useful coverage persisted, and where performance failed. A finite series establishes demonstrated breadth within those conditions, not universal tissue recognition. Claims of fewer errors, improved resection, preserved function or better outcomes should require additional clinical comparisons appropriate to each claimed benefit.
completion_criteria.label: Independent teams reproduce operative performance and report boundaries and failures

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: SUR-10, “Cell-identity-selective extirpation inside an organ that keeps working,” has the closest relationship. SUR-11 concerns seeing and identifying targets; SUR-10 concerns selectively removing them while maintaining organ function. Imaging could guide selective extirpation, but neither reliable removal nor preserved function follows from identification alone. The supplied roster title supports this distinction, although a detailed SUR-10 specification was not provided.

Roster-based synthesis: SUR-06, “Autonomous completion of whole operations at expert level,” could use continuous tissue identification as sensory input, but also requires operative decision-making and execution beyond imaging. SUR-07, “Incisionless resection and reconstruction inside the closed body,” concerns access and intervention; SUR-11 could potentially provide guidance in that setting, but does not itself supply incisionless access, resection or reconstruction.

Roster-based synthesis: SUR-01 and SUR-02 address transplant tolerance and xenotransplantation; SUR-03 addresses organ cryobanking; SUR-04 addresses restoration after complete spinal cord transection; SUR-05 addresses regenerative wound healing; SUR-08 addresses reversible metabolic arrest after traumatic exsanguination cardiac arrest; SUR-09 and SUR-12 address living replacements for complex parts and assembled autologous solid organs. Surgical imaging might assist procedures involving these advances, but their defining breakthroughs concern immunity, preservation, repair, physiological rescue or tissue construction. They remain distinct from continuous identification of the operative field, and their roster titles alone do not establish particular dependencies on SUR-11.

change_log.change: Separated cellular resolution, tissue identity, molecular specificity, perfusion and physiological function.
change_log.reason: Visible cellular detail does not by itself establish molecular identity or preserved function.

change_log.change: Qualified the 55–70 µm depth range and retained the review's separate discussion of approximately 250 µm superficial imaging.
change_log.reason: The smaller range cannot be generalized to every confocal system.

change_log.change: Corrected the 10.5-second measure to time to the first interpretable image and added enrollment dates and consultation scope.
change_log.reason: Image acquisition time is different from completed diagnostic turnaround, and consultation occurred in only 27 of 50 cases.

change_log.change: Preserved both conflicting overall sensitivity/specificity estimates, the margin/core difference and unresolved image and region counts.
change_log.reason: The supplied review identifies internal discrepancies without evidence that resolves them.

change_log.change: Integrated full-text support for motion and blood artifacts and explained the exclusion of uninterpretable regions.
change_log.reason: The finding no longer depends solely on a search excerpt, and diagnostic accuracy must be interpreted alongside imaging availability.

change_log.change: Retained the Raman study's reported quantitative and workflow claims with explicit extraction limitations.
change_log.reason: A cookie-only retained artifact prevents confirmation but does not justify declaring the findings false or deleting the research lead.

change_log.change: Made clinical benefits conditional and expanded proposed completion criteria to include unavailable coverage, reproducibility and practical boundaries.
change_log.reason: Technical identification performance does not establish improved outcomes, and finite testing cannot prove universal recognition.

change_log.change: Used the supplied roster to distinguish SUR-10 and other related entries, and preserved the unresolved freshness boundary.
change_log.reason: The roster supplies useful conceptual titles absent from the earlier review, while no supplied search establishes comprehensive field status through November 1, 2026.

unresolved_issues: Whether another modality or development through November 1, 2026 meets the full proposed scope remains unresolved because no usable freshness-search results were supplied.
The brain-tumor study's 93%/81% prose estimates and 92%/80% Table 3 estimates remain unreconciled, as do discrepancies in image and region counts.
The Raman study's identity, reported publication date, 70-case cohort, AUC of 0.77, processing time and single-specimen workflow could not be confirmed from the retained cookie-only extraction.
The intended operations, validated targets, field dimensions, depth, latency, performance targets and acceptable unavailable-imaging rates still require protocol-level definition.
Detailed specifications for the other roster entries were not supplied; related-concept comparisons are limited to their titles.

All substantive review recommendations were adopted. The review's inability to verify SUR-10's identity was partly addressed by the subsequently supplied roster title, while its detailed scope remains unverified.

brief.title: Live identification of tissue where surgeons cut
possible: During an operation, surgeons could see which cells, tissue types or specific molecules are present across the area where they are working, including where they are cutting. The display would update as tissue moves or is removed, without needing a removed sample for every reading.
why: When cancer spreads into normal tissue, its edges can be difficult to recognize. Continuous microscopic guidance could help surgeons locate remaining disease and reduce dependence on choosing the right spot to sample.
Identifying nerves, vessels and tissue boundaries could help surgeons choose where to cut and avoid critical structures.

sources.showed: Their review describes probe microscopy, which uses laser light to view cells inside the body. It helped identify abnormal digestive tissue, but covered small, shallow areas.
sources.quote:
In Barrett’s esophagus, adding pCLE to high-definition endoscopy nearly doubled 
neoplasia detection sensitivity versus standard protocols.
sources.cited_for: Microscopic imaging can help identify disease during a procedure.
sources.not_established: Small, superficial views do not establish continuous identification across the area being dissected.

sources.who: Yuan Xu and colleagues at Barrow Neurological Institute
sources.showed: At one hospital, a handheld laser microscope produced cellular images during brain surgery, including in gliomas, tumors that infiltrate brain tissue. Identifying tumor edges remained difficult.
sources.quote: Diagnostic performance was not statistically different between new and recurrent glioma cases or between glioma and other tumor types.
sources.cited_for: Surgeons can obtain cellular images at selected locations without removing tissue.
sources.not_established: The study did not demonstrate continuous guidance across the working area or improved surgical outcomes.

sources.who: Amin Nohman and colleagues at Heidelberg University Hospital
sources.showed: Their initial study used light to read tissue chemistry and AI to classify removed brain-tumor samples. They measured agreement with final diagnoses using AUC, a score of how well predictions distinguish diagnoses.
sources.quote: regression analysis showed an Area Under the Curve (AUC) of 0.77
sources.cited_for: Chemical imaging and automated interpretation can classify removed tissue during surgery.
sources.not_established: Testing removed samples does not establish continuous identification of tissue still in the body.

shown: A Barrow Neurological Institute feasibility study obtained cellular images during brain surgery in 50 patients. It examined selected spots with a handheld laser microscope. Identifying tumor edges was harder than identifying tissue within the tumor.
More than half of the acquired images were uninterpretable, commonly because of movement or clumped red blood cells. Regions without interpretable images were excluded from the diagnostic analysis.
missing: A system must combine useful area, depth, reliable identification and speed during active dissection.
The display must stay aligned as tissue moves, deforms or is removed.
Useful coverage must persist through blood and movement, with gaps clearly marked.
Identification must remain reliable where tumor and normal tissue intermingle.

milestones.label: Validated tissue identities across the cutting area
milestones.explanation: A human operation would have to demonstrate continuous, validated identification of cells or molecules across an area large enough to guide cutting without repeated sample removal. This would establish useful coverage during dissection.

milestones.label: Accuracy measured against tissue samples, including unusable areas
milestones.explanation: A planned human study would have to compare each relevant tissue type with microscopic examination of samples from matching locations and report unusable areas. This would reveal accuracy at difficult boundaries and gaps in coverage.

milestones.label: Independent teams reproduce performance and identify failures
milestones.explanation: Independent teams would have to reproduce performance across intended users, operations and conditions, reporting limits and failures. This would establish where guidance is dependable; patient benefits would need clinical comparisons.

uncertain: The required depth, area, update speed, accuracy and acceptable gaps still need definitions for each intended operation.
Recognizing nerves or vessels does not establish that nerves still carry signals or that vessels supply enough blood.
Whether this guidance would improve tumor removal, preserve function or improve patient outcomes remains open.

page.title: Real-time intraoperative cellular and molecular imaging
page.definition: An imaging system identifies cells, tissue types or molecular targets across the intact operative field, including the plane where tissue is being cut. Its spatial display updates during tissue manipulation and removal, without excising a specimen for each reading.

goal.need: In a 235-patient breast-conserving surgery trial, 21% needed another operation to clear the margin after usual surgery, compared with 10% when surgeons routinely removed an extra layer around the cavity. Final pathology can take days, and an optical biopsy examines only the chosen site. Locating cancer as tissue is cut could help surgeons remove it in one operation while sparing nearby nerves and vessels. False positives can lead to needless tissue removal, and a negative image can miss cancer.

statements.context: ARPA-H prefers whole-cavity coverage. Because motion and data volume may make it impractical, the programme also accepts imaging of regions selected by a defined rule.

completion.title: A human study validates continuous cellular or molecular identification across the operative field.
completion.criterion: For one specified operation and target class, a prospective human study meets registered diagnostic-performance endpoints while an integrated system identifies its targets across the intact working field, including the active cutting plane, during tissue manipulation and removal. Identification is validated against location-matched reference measurements. The protocol specifies area, depth, update latency, permitted coverage gaps and diagnostic thresholds. Acquisition does not require specimen removal for each reading.
completion.set_by: Atlas fallback; no external criterion defining this combined capability was found.
completion.basis: Searched ARPA-H PSI specifications, AAPM TG311, FDA device evaluations and clinical-study guidance, and ClinicalTrials.gov for a combined coverage, depth, latency and identification criterion during dissection. None located defines that test. PSI permits selected-region imaging; FDA’s Lumicell indication concerns imaging after primary excision. The fallback therefore tests one operation and target class in humans.

milestones.criterion: A prototype produces in vivo pathology images within the 30 min preparation-and-imaging allowance per region.
milestones.set_by: ARPA-H PSI solicitation, TA1-B Phase 1; GovTribe transcription.

milestones.title: Surgeons obtain optical biopsies in 90% of brain-tumour cases without excess adverse effects.
milestones.criterion: During brain-tumour surgery, the neurosurgeon obtains an optical biopsy by confocal laser endomicroscopy in 90% of cases. The number of adverse effects, including tissue injury or postoperative infection, does not exceed that in historical controls undergoing similar surgery without endomicroscopy.
milestones.set_by: Primary endpoints of the prospective Barrow Neurological Institute study, as reported by Xu and colleagues.
milestones.threshold_quote: confirming that the neurosurgeon could operate the CLE system to obtain noninvasive digital (i.e., optical) biopsies in 90% of cases.

milestones.title: Whole-cavity assessment in animals reaches ≥98% sensitivity and ≥95% specificity in under 10 minutes.
milestones.criterion: Test the integrated system in at least two cancer types using a rodent model and a large-animal model. Select prostate, breast or ovarian cancer as the first type. Evaluate the entire resection cavity in under 10 minutes, with 5 additional minutes allowed for preparation, at resolution of 0.5 μm or finer. Automated classification must locate any positive margin and reach ≥98% sensitivity and ≥95% specificity against one pathologist’s assessment of formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tissue.
milestones.set_by: ARPA-H PSI solicitation, TA1-B Phase 2, whole-cavity option; GovTribe transcription.
milestones.threshold_quote: Final sensitivity should be ≥98% and specificity ≥95%, demonstrated in relevant animal models of the chosen cancer.

milestones.title: FDA approves fluorescence imaging for residual breast cancer in the cavity after lumpectomy excision.
milestones.criterion: FDA approves an optical imaging agent and a fluorescence imaging device for use together in adults with breast cancer to help detect cancerous tissue in the lumpectomy cavity after the surgeon removes the primary specimen.
milestones.set_by: FDA, PMA P230014; the published indication is specific to breast lumpectomy.
milestones.threshold_quote: as an adjunct for the intraoperative detection of cancerous tissue within the resection cavity following removal of the primary specimen during lumpectomy surgery.

milestones.title: An integrated system displays cellular or molecular identities across the field during human dissection.
milestones.criterion: During authorised human feasibility testing, the integrated system produces a spatially registered identity display across the exposed working field, including the active cutting plane, while tissue is manipulated or removed. This establishes operation of the combined system in people; meeting prospective diagnostic-validation endpoints remains the completion test.
milestones.set_by: Atlas fallback: no external pass criterion for this combined functionality was found. FDA recognises early feasibility evaluation of clinical safety and device functionality.

milestones.title: An integrated in vivo microscope images a selected region within 10 minutes.
milestones.criterion: By programme month 48, the integrated device acquires an in vivo pathology image of a region of interest within 10 minutes. The allowance is for imaging time.
milestones.set_by: ARPA-H Precision Surgical Interventions solicitation, TA1-B Phase 2, month 48, as transcribed by GovTribe.
milestones.threshold_quote: Complete integrated device; region of interest (ROI) imaging time: 10 min/ROI (by month 48)

not_found: The original PSI solicitation attachment could not be opened through SAM.gov; its cited text is GovTribe’s transcription of the amendment dated 17 November 2023.

results.finding: In 50 brain-tumor surgery patients, the mean interval from fluorescein administration to CLE imaging was 40.1 min across sampled regions.
results.detail: The protocol scheduled fluorescein 5 minutes before imaging the first region. The pooled interval includes later regions and measures time from dosing to imaging, so it cannot establish the full per-region preparation-and-imaging time.
results.quote: For all ROIs, the mean (SD) time interval between FNa administration and CLE imaging was 40.1 (42.3) min.

results.finding: In 50 brain-tumor surgery patients, CLE acquired the first interpretable image of a selected region in a mean of 10.5 s after scan start.
results.quote: On average, the first interpretable images were acquired within 10.5 (25.3) s after the start of CLE imaging for each ROI.

results.finding: Neurosurgical teams obtained interpretable CLE optical biopsies in all 50 brain-tumor surgery patients.
results.detail: The reported safety results concern events attributed to imaging, contrast agents or probe use. The historical-control comparison is asserted in the endpoint summary without supporting comparator data.
results.quote: Interpretable CLE images were acquired from all 50 patients.

results.finding: In a 50-patient brain-tumor surgery study, real-time neuropathology interpretation of selected-site CLE images was performed in 27 cases.
results.detail: Neuronavigation provided location matching for sampled sites. The authors report that probe motion distorted images and that the scanning speed limited rapid inspection of large areas.
results.quote: The neuropathologist provided real-time image interpretation using a built-in telepathology consultation platform in 27 cases.

results.finding: EndoSCell imaged glioma resection cavities in vivo in a seven-rat guided-surgery group after 2 minutes of staining.
results.quote:
Methylene blue (1%) was locally perfused into the cavity for 2 min for
in vivo
staining. Following surgical removal, cell morphology and cellular patterns within the intracranial xenograft cavity were observed using EndoSCell.

results.finding: EndoSCell acquired in vivo surgical-margin images at 60 Hz in a seven-rat glioma guided-surgery group.
results.quote: It operates at a rapid frame rate of 60 Hz, delivering exceptionally stable real-time images from the surgical margin, thanks to its autofocus capability.

results.finding: EndoSCell scanned the full glioma resection cavity for positive margins in a seven-rat guided-surgery group after 2 minutes of staining.
results.detail: An endoscopist and a pathologist jointly evaluated the images. Postoperative histology assessed residual tumor or recurrence and supplied no margin-level sensitivity or specificity estimates.
results.quote: The entire cavity was scanned to locate any positive margins, which were then refined until a safe negative margin was confirmed.

results.finding: Prototype Lumicell DVS distinguished cancer from normal tissue in 92% of canine biopsies. The biopsy count was unreported.
FDA approved Lumicell DVS for use with LUMISIGHT on April 17, 2024. The pivotal efficacy cohort included 357 patients.
results.quote: CDRH issued an approval order on April 17, 2024.

results.finding: In the Phase C IDE feasibility study, 230 patients completed intraoperative Lumicell DVS imaging of the lumpectomy cavity.
results.quote: A total of 230 patients completed the study in the mITT Population (Table 15).

results.finding: SLIMBRAIN displayed registered tissue maps at 14 frames per second during brain tumor surgery, with hyperspectral sequences evaluated from five patients.
results.detail: The display classified tissue using hyperspectral signatures. The study evaluated held-out pixels from the same patients used for training against neurosurgeon labels. Histopathological comparison was planned.
results.quote:
This system captures and processes HS images at 14 frames per second (FPS) during the course of a tumor
resection operation to detect and delimit cancer tissue at the same time the neurosurgeon operates.

results.finding: MediSCAPE acquired in vivo oral histology images in one healthy volunteer, with scans lasting up to 120 s.
results.detail: Preparation included a water rinse and positioning the tissue against a sterile imaging cap. The paper gives no duration for those steps.

results.finding: Miniaturized MediSCAPE acquired an in vivo lip scan showing histological features in 25 s in one healthy volunteer.
results.detail: The 25 s measures image acquisition. The authors stitched and rendered the acquired data offline.
results.quote: Comparable stitched roving scan from miniaturized MediSCAPE system from regions C to D (25 s at 4.8 VPS, 6 mm long).

results.finding: MediSCAPE mapped up to 13 mm of intact oral tissue in one healthy volunteer using offline stitching.
results.detail: The experiment demonstrated acquisition and reconstruction in a person. It did not test an operative identity display during tissue manipulation or removal.
results.quote: Importantly, large areas of the tissue of interest, here stitched to up to 13 mm for demonstration, can be canvassed for early detection of suspicious lesions and non-invasive follow-up and monitoring.

results.finding: In 11 glioma patients, intraoperative EGFR-targeted fluorescence had a mean contrast-to-noise ratio of 9.5 at MRI contrast-enhancing sites.
results.detail: The overlays mapped fluorescence intensity. Histology confirmed sampled residual tumor, and cellular localization was assessed on excised tissue sections.
results.quote: Intraoperative fluorescence improved optical contrast in tumor tissue within and beyond the T1 contrast-enhancing margin, with contrast-to-noise ratios of 9.5 ± 2.1 and 3.6 ± 1.1, respectively.

results.finding: The fluorescence-enabled operative microscope imaged residual glioma during resection in 1 patient.
results.detail: The microscope used its INFRARED 800 mode to visualize fluorescence from panitumumab-IRDye800 in the wound bed.
results.quote: To streamline the intraoperative fluorescence visualization within the surgical workflow, a neurosurgical microscope equipped with an appropriate filter (INFRARED 800) was adopted to detect NIR fluorescence simultaneously as ongoing resection

results.finding: Handheld quantitative phase microscopy imaged five skin regions in one healthy volunteer and six brain regions in one healthy swine in vivo at 25 frames per second.
results.detail: Both in vivo demonstrations used healthy tissue. Tumor histopathology was demonstrated on excised mouse and human brain tissue.
results.quote: The handheld probe presented here is a fully integrated, epi quantitative phase imaging system capable of real-time (25 Hz), wide-field, non-scanning subcellular imaging in vivo.

results.finding: Among 210 adults enrolled for intracranial lesion resection, intraoperative confocal laser endomicroscopy yielded images assessed in 203 cases.
results.detail: Seven enrollees were excluded from the full analysis set. Two withdrew before surgery, two had device failures, and three lacked adequate frozen sections. The full analysis set therefore provides a minimum acquisition count for the enrolled cohort.
results.quote: The digital projection of the CLE imaging was evaluated centrally by a trained neuropathologist (J.S.) for all participating centers after surgery.

results.finding: AKRO-QC-ICG hydrogel imaging detected breast cancer with 94% spot-level sensitivity in 10 mice bearing patient-derived xenografts.
results.detail: Researchers manually inked high-fluorescence areas and compared selected spots with H&E cryosections. The 10-minute incubation preceded rinsing and image acquisition.
results.quote: The in vivo efficacy of the AKRO-QC-ICG imaging gel to detect BCa revealed the levels of sensitivity/specificity = 0.92/1 in 12 nude mice, which was corroborated with the sensitivity/specificity = 0.94/1 in 10 PDX mice.

results.finding: Intraoperative fluorescence imaging of 10 canine tumor resections in nine dogs agreed with margin histopathology in nine of 10 cases.
results.detail: The discordant case was a false negative. No residual fluorescence was seen, but histology found tumor at the margin.
results.quote: Histopathologic assessment of surgical margins correlated with intraoperative imaging in nine of 10 cases; in the other case, there was no residual fluorescence, but tumor was found at the margin on histologic examination.

results.finding: In 25 patients undergoing tumor resection, the live PpIX overlay matched conventional blue-light fluorescence in all 26 resections.
results.detail: The surgeon judged agreement visually. The study included no spatially matched histopathology of regions with different fluorescence intensities.
results.quote: In all 26 surgeries, we were able to correlate the pink fluorescence under blue light with the “green” fluorescence in the MFL-mode.

goal.need = "In a 235-patient breast-conserving surgery trial, 21% needed another operation to clear the margin after usual surgery, compared with 10% when surgeons routinely removed an extra layer around the cavity. Final pathology can take days, and an optical biopsy examines only the chosen site. Locating cancer as tissue is cut could help surgeons remove it in one operation while sparing nearby nerves and vessels. False positives can lead to needless tissue removal, and a negative image can miss cancer.". Reason: The current rationale counts unusable images but omits the burden of repeat surgery and the consequences of missing cancer or removing healthy tissue.

add statement by Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health, Precision Surgical Interventions solicitation, in vivo pathology track, 2023: "image the entire resection cavity at microscopic resolution". Reason: The solicitation states how much tissue ARPA-H wanted to image and makes explicit the alternative it would accept.

edit m2: title = "Surgeons obtain optical biopsies in 90% of brain-tumour cases without excess adverse effects."; criterion = "During brain-tumour surgery, the neurosurgeon obtains an optical biopsy by confocal laser endomicroscopy in 90% of cases. The number of adverse effects, including tissue injury or postoperative infection, does not exceed that in historical controls undergoing similar surgery without endomicroscopy."; set_by = "Primary endpoints of the prospective Barrow Neurological Institute study, as reported by Xu and colleagues."; threshold_quote = "confirming that the neurosurgeon could operate the CLE system to obtain noninvasive digital (i.e., optical) biopsies in 90% of cases."; threshold_ref = 1; refs = [1]. Reason: The title generalizes a brain-tumour endpoint to all operations, and the criterion mixes the study’s test with its results.

edit m3: title = "Whole-cavity assessment in animals reaches \u226598% sensitivity and \u226595% specificity in under 10 minutes."; criterion = "Test the integrated system in at least two cancer types using a rodent model and a large-animal model. Select prostate, breast or ovarian cancer as the first type. Evaluate the entire resection cavity in under 10 minutes, with 5 additional minutes allowed for preparation, at resolution of 0.5 \u03bcm or finer. Automated classification must locate any positive margin and reach \u226598% sensitivity and \u226595% specificity against one pathologist\u2019s assessment of formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tissue."; threshold_quote = "Final sensitivity should be \u226598% and specificity \u226595%, demonstrated in relevant animal models of the chosen cancer."; threshold_ref = 5; refs = [5]. Reason: The whole-cavity test requires automated classification and localization of positive margins, and its time limit is strictly less than 10 minutes.
